explanation: For business meetings, Greek professionals are expected to arrive on time — a leading etiquette guide explicitly advises punctuality for meetings, even though the meeting's pace may still run flexibly once underway. Social gatherings are different: Greece, like other Mediterranean cultures, follows a more relaxed, relationship-first sense of time where arriving somewhat late to a casual dinner or party is common and rarely offends.
local_tip: Arrive on time (or only a few minutes late) for business meetings; for a casual dinner or party invitation, arriving 15-30 minutes after the stated time is normal and not considered rude.

also_check.note: Lateness is seen as unprofessional and a sign of poor planning, especially for business.
Punctuality is critical for both business and most social plans; even a few minutes late is notable.
Arriving somewhat late to social gatherings is similarly common and accepted, though business punctuality is expected.
